clue.text: Like some dogs, raced around too much

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, wrapping it on both sides

parts.note: raced means went fast, sped
OTT is short for over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Dogs that dash about wildly, as some breeds are said to do.
explanation.walkthrough: SPED is split to hold OTT, the abbreviation for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatians and other breeds have a coat marked with spots, so they are spotted.

clue.text: Network stop second director working

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Jacques Tati, the French film director
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A film director gets off at the second stop on the transport network.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a place where trains on a rail network halt to pick up passengers.

clue.text: Get through more cash than English pounds, tons need changing

indicators.note: letters that need changing must be put into a different order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Someone overspending in sterling, worried that their money must be exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To outspend someone is to spend more money than they do, getting through more cash.

clue.text: A lot of land agreement has no disadvantage

indicators.note: has no means a part is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement
a con is a drawback, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A land deal drawn up with no downside for either party.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTRACT loses CON, the drawback from pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a large expanse or area of land or territory.

clue.text: Decide to put off excavation

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
a mine is a dug-out excavation

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to postpone the dig.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine something is to settle or resolve it, a synonym of decide.

clue.text: Record single back around number four in chart

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: single means alone, lone

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the following word is the one kept

parts.note: the fourth letter of chart

explanation.surface: A lone single climbing back to number four in the music charts.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to enter a name on a register, to record someone officially.

clue.text: Yet I'm upset about new animosity

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following piece
something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of these words
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are still upset about something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or ill will between people, the same as animosity.

clue.text: Something to see in the Capitol and tour around

definitions.text: Something to see in the Capitol

indicators.note: letters moved around end up in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A sightseer's advice to visit Washington's Capitol and look about.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed circular hall at the heart of the US Capitol building is famous as a sight for visitors.

clue.text: Look briefly to dispatch good weapon

indicators.note: to dispatch something is to send it away, so it is removed

parts.note: a glance is a brief look
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A quick glance before finishing off an opponent with a good weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight, an old weapon.

clue.text: What might kill something like albatross over front of ship

parts.note: in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the albatross is hung about the mariner's neck instead of the cross
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: The Ancient Mariner's crossbow, which shot the albatross from the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second. Coleridge's mariner kills the albatross with a crossbow, so the whole clue tells his story.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a weapon that shoots bolts, so it is something that might kill.

clue.text: Respond with about turn

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a turn is a performance on stage, an act

explanation.surface: An instruction to answer by doing an about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' looks like the drill command, but splits into two words with separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something that has happened.

clue.text: Machine boxing fruit in gold November

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing something as in a box

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
N is November in the NATO alphabet
the tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A device packing autumn fruit in golden November light.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold and November together surround the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, often one built to imitate a person.

clue.text: Scrap — small dog perhaps grabs bite

indicators.note: something that grabs another thing holds it inside its grip

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a dog is one example of a pet
a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: A fight with a little dog that snaps at you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, but here it means a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment, just like a scrap.

clue.text: Uniform carried by entire travelling entourage

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it
letters that are travelling move about and change places

parts.note: the letters of this word
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A whole touring party in matching uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who accompany an important person, an entourage.

clue.text: Block an interrogation to eliminate last cause of slippage

indicators.note: eliminating the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to ban is to block or prohibit
taken as written
asking questions is interrogation

explanation.surface: Someone stopping a police interview to cut short its final part.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is the classic slapstick cause of a fall, and figuratively a cause of embarrassing blunders.

clue.text: In a long line getting beer round bar

indicators.note: round means placed around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
a rung is a bar of a ladder

explanation.surface: A long queue at the pub, with drinkers getting a round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' and 'bar' look like pub words, but one is a container signal and the other a ladder part.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strung out are spread in a long straggling line.

clue.text: Perhaps ammonia has power to catch the breath

parts.note: ammonia is one example of a gas
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: The strong smell of ammonia making someone choke.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw a sudden sharp breath, to catch the breath.

clue.text: A rhyme is troublesome

parts.note: a, as in 'once a week', means per
a rhyme is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A poet finding a rhyme hard to get right.
explanation.walkthrough: The innocent-looking 'A' is a word in its own right: 'a' can mean per, as in sixty miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary or awkward, deliberately causing difficulty.

clue.text: Who'll show climate turning endlessly severe?

definitions.text: Who'll show climate turning endlessly severe?

indicators.note: turning means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the climate or atmosphere in a place is its mood

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: stern means severe

explanation.surface: Asking who predicts that the climate will become ever harsher.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a prophet of disaster, while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doomster is a pessimist who forecasts catastrophe, such as a dire climate future.

clue.text: Properly healthy spa

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a proper or satisfactory way
third meaning: a spring of mineral water

explanation.surface: A truly health-giving spa resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word, an adverb, an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means satisfactorily, means in good health, and names a spring, as in Tunbridge Wells.

clue.text: Ship's rope in dock holding beam up

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside

parts.note: to dock is to come to land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A ship's rope used in dock to hoist a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short rope on a ship used for securing or rigging.

clue.text: Docker perhaps not working is a sponger

parts.note: someone not working is free
a docker is one example of someone who loads ships

explanation.surface: An idle dock worker accused of living off others.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in the opposite order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader lives off others' generosity without paying, a sponger.

clue.text: Vague about Indian city plan

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: dim means vague or indistinct
Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Someone hazy about the layout of a city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing that shows the layout of something, a plan.

clue.text: Spring back with green during more than half of April

indicators.note: more than half keeps most of the word and loses the rest
during means within the span of the next piece

parts.note: the last three of its five letters
eco- means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: Plants springing back into green growth in April.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring or jump back, as a gun does when fired.

clue.text: Restaurant initially needs support in Canada

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: CAN is the abbreviation for Canada

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of needs
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A Canadian restaurant that first needs some backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining room serving meals in a workplace or school.

clue.text: Secretive egret regularly hides in island

indicators.note: something that hides in another sits inside it

parts.note: a cay is a low island

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A shy egret concealing itself on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A cay, or key, is a small low island of sand or coral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cagey is guarded and unwilling to give information, secretive.

clue.text: Anger about some current wild behaviour

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Fury over some modern trend in reckless conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day', but it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a period of violent, uncontrolled behaviour.

clue.text: Nothing in France holds society up

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside

parts.note: rien is French for nothing
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A French society where nothing gets held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has risen is up, out of bed or on their feet.

clue.text: Girl on the outside loving and beautifully attractive

indicators.note: on the outside means only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of girl
amorous means loving

explanation.surface: A girl who is affectionate and gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous describes someone strikingly and stylishly attractive.

clue.text: Ring modulator usually features

indicators.note: the phrase features the answer, containing it within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A ring modulator, an electronic music effect, is usually part of a setup.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is the ring or doughnut shape in geometry.

clue.text: Sing free melody without metre

indicators.note: letters set free can be rearranged in any order
without means the following part is left out

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for metre

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing a free-flowing tune with no fixed rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metre' suggests poetic rhythm, but it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between normal voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Pet insect runs in bread basket

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: bread basket is slang for the stomach, the tum
an ant is an insect
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pet beetle scurrying around in the bread bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal, but a pet is also a sulk or fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a childish fit of bad temper, which is what a pet means in old British usage.
